memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Avery secured only the fixed Sunday outbound after comparing arrival margin and disruption recovery. Thursday return options were evaluated against several possible lender-signoff end times, but no return was purchased or held because the schedule remains uncertain.

messages.content: I need to start planning a Philadelphia work trip. I have a mount inspection at 9:00 Monday morning, so I want to fly from Atlanta on Sunday and be settled in Philadelphia well before the evening. The lender signoff is Thursday, but I do not have its end time yet.

What dates are Sunday and Thursday, and are you looking for economy? I can compare the outbound first, then map Thursday returns around a few possible signoff times without purchasing that uncertain leg.
Sunday, October 18, through Thursday, October 22, 2026. Economy is fine. The exhibition components are going by truck, so I will only have a carry-on and a small personal bag.

For Sunday, October 18, I found three nonstop economy options from Atlanta to Philadelphia: Delta at 10:05 a.m., arriving 12:08 p.m., for $214 one way; American at 12:35 p.m., arriving 2:39 p.m., for $187; and Delta at 3:10 p.m., arriving 5:14 p.m., for $176. All times are local. The morning Delta gives you the most settling time, while the American flight is the lower-priced option that still arrives by midafternoon.
The 3:10 arrival option is later than I want. Compare the first two more closely, including what happens if there is a delay.

The 10:05 Delta is scheduled to arrive 2 hours 31 minutes earlier than the American flight. It also has later nonstop Delta departures at 12:20 p.m., 3:10 p.m., and 5:45 p.m. that could serve as same-day alternatives if the original flight is disrupted and seats are available. The 12:35 American has later nonstops at 3:25 p.m. and 6:05 p.m. Both fares include a standard carry-on; checked baggage would cost extra. Neither schedule creates a guarantee against delays, but the morning departure leaves substantially more recovery room before Sunday evening.
Use the 10:05 Delta as the outbound. Now show me Thursday possibilities. The signoff might finish at 1:00, but it could run until 3:30 or even 4:00. I will be at the museum near the Parkway.

Allowing roughly 30 minutes to close out your work, 25 to 40 minutes to reach PHL in ordinary traffic, and time for security, a 1:00 p.m. finish could support a departure around 4:00 p.m. or later. If signoff runs to 3:30 or 4:00, departures before about 6:30 would be risky. Relevant nonstop returns are Delta at 4:25 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 6:43 p.m.; American at 5:40 p.m., arriving 7:58 p.m.; Delta at 7:05 p.m., arriving 9:23 p.m.; and American at 8:15 p.m., arriving 10:33 p.m.
What do those cost when paired with the Sunday Delta? I am not ready to buy the return because the lender has not confirmed the schedule.

With the Sunday 10:05 a.m. Delta outbound, the all-Delta round trip is currently $368 with the 4:25 p.m. return or $391 with the 7:05 p.m. return. Pairing it with American on a separate return ticket brings the combined current price to $354 for the 5:40 p.m. flight or $376 for the 8:15 p.m. flight. Separate tickets would mean separate change and disruption handling, so the all-Delta combinations are operationally simpler.
The 4:25 is obviously only useful if we finish at 1:00. Is 7:05 realistic if we finish at 4:00?

Yes, but it is not generous. If you leave the museum around 4:30, an ordinary drive could put you at the airport between 4:55 and 5:10, about two hours before departure. A traffic problem or a delayed closeout would reduce that margin. The 8:15 American adds 70 minutes, though it requires the separate-ticket combination and gets you to Atlanta after 10:30 p.m.
I would rather keep the 7:05 Delta in view. Can you hold the round trip while I wait for the lender?

Delta is not offering a multi-day complimentary hold on this fare. The itinerary can be saved to your trip list at the current schedule, but that does not protect the $391 price or reserve a seat. Another option is to buy the Sunday outbound alone for $214 and leave the Thursday flight unpurchased. The 7:05 return is currently $177 one way, so that would equal the same $391 total at today's prices.
Could we purchase the whole round trip and change the Thursday flight later without a penalty?

The quoted Main Cabin fare has no airline change fee, but you would owe any fare difference when switching flights. A lower replacement fare would generally become an eCredit rather than a cash refund. If you canceled instead, the ticket value would also be retained as an eCredit under the displayed terms. A refundable round trip is $612 and can be returned to the original payment method, but that is $221 more.
Do not purchase the return yet. I do need the Sunday flight secured, though. Before doing that, check whether the one-way fare is Main Cabin rather than Basic Economy and whether I can choose a seat.

The $214 one-way fare is Delta Main Cabin, booking class T. Seat selection is included, subject to availability, and the ticket can be changed without an airline change fee, with a fare difference if applicable. Basic Economy is also displayed at $169, but it has tighter change and seat-assignment restrictions.
Stay with Main Cabin. What seats are open?

On the 10:05 a.m. nonstop, standard seats currently available include 16A and 16F by the windows, 17C and 17D on the aisles, and several middle seats in rows 18 through 21. Preferred seats closer to the front begin at an additional $24. The aircraft shown is an Airbus A321, and the flight is scheduled for 2 hours 3 minutes.

Select 17C and book only that outbound. Then save the 7:05 Thursday return as the leading option, with the 8:15 American noted as the fallback. Please be very clear that neither return is being purchased.

Before ticketing, the total for the Delta one-way Main Cabin flight is $214.00, including taxes and fees. It departs ATL at 10:05 a.m. Sunday, October 18, and arrives PHL at 12:08 p.m. Seat 17C is selected. Shall I complete that purchase using the payment method on file ending in 4821?
Yes, complete the $214 outbound purchase.

The outbound is ticketed. Delta confirmation G7Q4LM covers one passenger on Sunday, October 18, 2026, departing Atlanta at 10:05 a.m. and arriving Philadelphia at 12:08 p.m. in Main Cabin, seat 17C. The charged total is $214.00. For Thursday, October 22, I saved notes for the Delta 7:05 p.m. nonstop as the leading option and the American 8:15 p.m. nonstop as the fallback. Neither Thursday flight is reserved, held, or purchased, and their fares and availability may change before you decide.
